program_name: Cognitive Science and Theory of Communication
degree_class: LM-55-R - Scienze cognitive / LM-92-R - Teorie della comunicazione (interclass degree)
academic_requirements: Access is free (no numerus clausus), but curricular preparation is verified before enrolment by an evaluation committee, per the course regulations. Enrolment requires a three-year (Bachelor's) degree in one of the following classes: L-05 (Philosophy), L-19 (Education and training sciences), L-20 (Communication sciences), L-24 (Psychological sciences and techniques), L-15 (Cultural tourism), L-03 D.A.M.S. (Performing arts), L-39 (Social service sciences), L-31 (Computer sciences and technologies), or equivalent; OR another three-year Italian degree that guarantees at least 30 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors: Linguistics (L-LIN/01), Education Sciences (M-PED), Philosophy (M-FIL), Psychology and Neurosciences (M-PSI), Social Sciences (SPS), Computer Sciences and Computer Engineering (INF, ING-INF); OR a foreign degree recognised as suitable. Candidates are expected to have in-depth knowledge of cognitive processes, methodology of empirical sciences, and adequate notions of neuroscience, philosophy, semiotics, communication, pedagogy, anthropology, linguistics, IT and socio-political fields.
language_requirements: As this is an international course taught in English, the programme's own admission page states a minimum English competence level of B1 (CEFR) is required as an entry qualification. This differs from the general UniME university-wide rule for English-taught programmes, which requires an International English Language Certificate at CEFR B2 level (IELTS 5.5+, TOEFL iBT 72+, Cambridge English B2 First+, PTE General Level 3, or PTE Academic 59+, unless exempt) uploaded to the language section of the UniME Application Portal. This B1-vs-B2 discrepancy between the programme page and the general portal rule could not be resolved from official sources and is flagged as uncertain. No specific Italian-language requirement applies to this English-taught programme.
entry_exam_or_test: No formal written entrance exam is specified. 'The verification of the student's preparation is carried out prior to enrolment in accordance with the procedures indicated in the course regulations' — i.e., a document-based curricular evaluation by an evaluation committee, consistent with the general UNIME Master's admission process (preliminary evaluation application via Esse3/UniME Application Portal, assessed by a Departmental Commission).
required_documents: High School Diploma (obtained after at least 12 years of education, or official provisional certificate if not yet issued)
Bachelor's Degree diploma or official provisional certificate issued by the university (candidate must show at least 15 years of total education)
Transcript of records (exams passed in the previous degree programme)
English language certificate (B1 per the programme page; B2 per the general UniME rule for English-taught programmes — see language_requirements) or proof of exemption
Universitaly pre-enrolment application (for visa-required non-EU applicants, submitted after receiving the UniME admission letter)
application_deadline_eu: [uncertain] Applicable university-wide 2026/2027 rounds relevant to EU/EU-equivalent/no-visa applicants: '6th Call - No Visa Applicants' (Italians with foreign qualification, EU and EU-equivalent candidates) - from 1 July 2026 (00:01 CEST) to 20 November 2026 (23:59 CET), covering English-taught & Italian-taught Bachelor's and Master's Degrees. A non-refundable EUR 30.00 application fee applies (covers up to two applications across calls). These are university-wide calls (from international.unime.it), not published separately on the programme's own cdl.unime.it site.
application_deadline_non_eu: [uncertain] For non-EU (Study VISA) applicants, three sequential rounds apply to Master's programmes for the 2026/2027 intake: '1st Call - Early Bird' from 24 November 2025 (00:01 CET) to 22 December 2025 (23:59 CET); '2nd Call - Visa Applicants' from 1 February 2026 (00:01 CET) to 31 March 2026 (23:59 CEST); '3rd Call - Visa Applicants' from 13 April 2026 (00:01 CEST) to 10 May 2026 (23:59 CEST). Non-refundable EUR 30.00 application fee (covers up to two applications). After a positive evaluation, applicants receive an admission letter and must register on Universitaly (UNIME confirms acceptance there) to start the visa process; for a.y. 2026/2027 the Universitaly deadline is stated as 1 September 2026. Two-portal flow: UniME Application Portal (pre-evaluation) then Universitaly (visa confirmation).
